headline: Custer Gallatin Wilderness and Hyalite Reservation Brief
reservation: Wilderness entry is generally open, but developed campgrounds like those in Hyalite Canyon or near Big Sky require advance booking via Recreation.gov. Specialized permits are mandatory for certain commercial activities or large groups; always check the official Custer Gallatin National Forest site for seasonal fire closures or bear-related restrictions.

days.title: Canyons and Cascades

stops.name: Palisade Falls
stops.detail: Walk the paved trail in Hyalite Canyon to see a massive vertical drop over unique basalt columns.

stops.name: Hyalite Reservoir
stops.detail: Experience non-motorized recreation at this high-altitude basin surrounded by rugged peaks.

days.driving: Allow 60-90 minutes; road conditions vary by snowmelt
days.note: Hyalite Canyon road has seasonal closures; verify access before departing.

days.title: Rivers and Ridges

stops.name: Gallatin River
stops.detail: Observe world-class fly fishing water in the narrow limestone gorge where 'A River Runs Through It' was filmed.

stops.name: Ousel Falls Park
stops.detail: A well-maintained trail leading to a powerful waterfall, perfect for experiencing the Gallatin Range's hydrology.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; watch for wildlife on Highway 191
days.note: Expect heavy traffic on the 191 corridor during peak ski or summer seasons.

days.title: Alpine Tundra and High Passes

stops.name: Hebgen Lake
stops.detail: Explore the site of the historic 1959 earthquake and the surrounding mountain views.

stops.name: Grizzly & Wolf Discovery Center
stops.detail: Visit this accredited facility to learn about the apex predators that inhabit the surrounding forest.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary with weather
days.note: High elevation weather changes rapidly; carry layers even in mid-summer.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Hyalite Canyon lots often reach capacity by 9 AM during summer weekends. Have a secondary trail in mind if primary lots are restricted by Forest Service staff.

intel.title: Remote Wilderness Blackouts
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent in much of the Gallatin Canyon and high alpine basins. Carry a satellite communicator or physical maps for navigation beyond main road corridors.

intel.title: Mountain Gateway Services
intel.text: Fuel is available in Bozeman, Big Sky, and West Yellowstone, but absent within the forest interior. Ensure a full tank before entering the Hebgen Lake or Hyalite areas.

intel.title: Seasonal Mud and Snow
intel.text: High altitude trails may remain snow-covered until July; 'mud season' in May can lead to temporary trail closures to prevent erosion. Check the Gallatin National Forest avalanche center in winter.

intel.title: Grizzly Habitat Protocols
intel.text: The entire forest is active bear territory; carry bear spray in an accessible holster and know the proper storage regulations for food. Check for emergency closures due to wildlife activity.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at Bozeman (BZN) or Cody (COD); stock up on bear-safe storage containers in town before heading to mountain trailheads.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for forest service roads; check rental contracts for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Gallatin Canyon overlooks for late afternoon light; verify local sunset times as canyon walls create early shadows.
